messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@vitalitylabs.com>, Tom Serrano <t.serrano@vitalitylabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC boarding: Action compact — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist, peering

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thank you for the time yesterday. Per our mutual action plan discussion I’m sharing a compact POC onboarding checklist so we can agree on owners and dates and unblock the environment setup. Attached: map-action-compact-v1.xlsx and a simple VPC diagram.

High-level asks to get us into a testable POC in your staging account:
- Org & admin invite: Vitality will create a customer org and add redwood-bot@redwood.ai (or invite marissa.cole@redwood.ai) as a deployment/observer admin. Owner: Vitality.
- API keys: Redwood will provision a read-only ephemeral API key for initial smoke runs; Vitality needs to confirm any KMS/HSM restrictions. Owner: Redwood ops / Vitality security.
- IP allowlist: Vitality to provide CIDR ranges for the staging hosts that will call the API (we’ll add these to the VPC endpoint allowlist). Example: 34.82.128.0/20.
- VPC peering: Proposed peering window: Wed 6/12 2200–0100 PDT (low-traffic); we’ll coordinate the route table update and test harness.

Proposed milestone dates (draft):
1) 6/05 — Org created and initial invite accepted
2) 6/07 — CIDR ranges shared and API key request submitted
3) 6/12 — VPC peering established and smoke tests run
4) 6/14 — Canary workload and perf validation complete

Please review and flag any blockers. If this looks good I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet with owners and push a formal row-by-row signoff column so we can track acceptance.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0129
Redwood Inference

Attachments: map-action-compact-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), vpc-peering-diagram.png (PNG)

Subject: Re: POC boarding: Action compact — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist, peering

Marissa — thanks, this is clear and appreciated. A couple of items from our side:

- Org owner: I’ll create the Vitality-staging org today and invite marissa.cole@redwood.ai as a deployment observer. Internal owner: Aisha (Infra).
- CIDRs: our staging egress will come from these ranges: 34.82.144.0/22, 35.201.0.0/16 — we can narrow further if needed. We’ll provide a short justification note for security.
- KMS: we use an in-house KMS for production but staging is OK without HSM for now — no blocking by security. If you require specific headers for key exchange let us know.
- Peering window: Wed 6/12 22:00 PDT works for infra; please put a 60-min buffer for rollback.

Action item: Tom will coordinate procurement for the PO/doc signoff; I’m looping him on timing.

Can you confirm the format you want for the API key rotation policy and whether the ephemeral key TTL can be set to 8 hours for the canary?

Best,
Aisha
VP, Infra — Vitality Labs
aisha.patel@vitalitylabs.com

Quick tech note:
- For peering we’ll need a single routing prefix on your side for the initial test (the /22 is fine). Please confirm whether the peered subnet overlaps with any existing CIDRs (we cannot accept overlapping ranges).
- API key plan: we’ll issue an ephemeral key with 8 hour TTL scoped to the staging org and an allowlist of the CIDRs you provide. Keys are rotated server-side; we’ll publish the key id and fingerprint to your security contact via the MAP spreadsheet.
- Service accounts: please create a service account with the least privilege for the canary (token creation + read-only inference). We can do a live walkthrough if your infra team prefers.

I’ll prepare an abbreviated runbook for Wed 6/12 that lists the exact CLI commands and verification checks (BGP/route table edits not necessary — just route table + security group updates).

— Karthik
Sr. Infra Eng — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks — consolidating and proposing a signed-off timeline so procurement and infra all have clear dates. Please review and reply with approvals or changes by EOD Friday 6/07.

Updated milestone plan (final draft for signoff):
- 6/01 (today): Vitality org created, invite accepted by Redwood (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) — DONE/IN PROGRESS
- 6/04: Vitality shares final CIDR allowlist and any KMS constraints (owner: Vitality infra)
- 6/07: Redwood posts ephemeral API key request in MAP and provides rotation policy doc (owner: Redwood ops)
- 6/12 22:00–23:30 PDT: VPC peering, route updates, smoke test (owner: Redwood infra + Vitality infra)
- 6/14: Canary validation complete; pass/fail entry in MAP; if pass => proceed to evaluation runs (owner: both)

Open questions / acceptance criteria:
- Ephemeral API TTL: Aisha requested 8 hours. Redwood approves for canary; production TTL will be negotiated separately.
- Rollback window: 60 minutes post-peering (documented in runbook).
- Security evidence: Vitality to confirm whether a short SOC2 scoping doc is required for the staging peering; if yes we’ll mark the MAP row as pending procurement.

If everyone is OK I’ll add a Sign-off column to the spreadsheet and mark rows ready for a simple approval (text reply ok).

Thanks,
Marissa
